name: Drupal
tagline: A flexible, secure enterprise content management system.
timeTravelLog: Created by Dries Buytaert in 2000 as a student message board, Drupal evolved into one of the most widely used content management systems — powering government portals, university systems, and multinational enterprise platforms.
overview: Drupal is an open-source content management system written in PHP. It is renowned for its flexibility, security, and scalability — powering complex web applications that require granular access control, custom data structures, and multi-site architectures.

syllabus.title: Module 1: Drupal Architecture Overview
syllabus.desc: Understanding Drupal's layered architecture of core, modules, and themes.
syllabus.content: Drupal's architecture consists of four layers: Core (the engine — routing, database, caching), Modules (feature plugins that extend functionality), Themes (presentation layer — HTML/CSS/Twig templates), and Configuration (YAML-based exported site settings). Everything in Drupal is a plugin — even field types, views, and user roles are plugins defined through annotations and YAML.
syllabus.codeExample:
/* Drupal Directory Structure */
/web
  /core          ← Drupal core (never modify!)
  /modules
    /contrib     ← Community modules (downloaded)
    /custom      ← Your custom modules
  /themes
    /contrib     ← Community themes
    /custom      ← Your custom theme
  /sites
    /default
      settings.php     ← Database & config
      /files           ← Uploaded media
composer.json          ← Dependency manager
syllabus.interactiveTip: Never modify files inside /core — it will break on the next Drupal update! All customization belongs in /modules/custom and /themes/custom directories exclusively.

syllabus.title: Module 2: Content Types & Field Architecture
syllabus.desc: Structuring your data model with Drupal's entity and field system.
syllabus.content: In Drupal, structured content is built via Content Types — reusable data blueprints (like Project Report, Case Study, Blog Post). Each content type is composed of Fields (text, image, date, entity reference, etc.) configured through the admin UI or YAML config. Paragraphs module enables flexible, nested content layouts. Field formatters control how data renders in views.
syllabus.codeExample:
# Exported content type config (YAML)
# config/sync/node.type.project_report.yml
id: project_report
label: 'Project Report'
description: 'Internal project field documentation'
new_revision: true
preview_mode: 1

# Field definition
# config/sync/field.field.node.project_report.field_access.yml
entity_type: node
bundle: project_report
field_name: field_access
label: 'Access Level'
required: true
syllabus.interactiveTip: Export all config via drush config-export after making changes in the admin UI. Store config YAML in version control — this enables reproducible site builds and team collaboration!

syllabus.title: Module 3: Views (The Data Query Builder)
syllabus.desc: Building dynamic, filtered, paginated content displays without SQL queries.
syllabus.content: Views is Drupal's most powerful contrib module (included in core since Drupal 8). It provides a visual query builder that fetches content and renders it as lists, tables, grids, blocks, or JSON feeds. Every listing on a typical Drupal site is a View — recent posts, user tables, taxonomy term pages, and REST API endpoints.
syllabus.codeExample:
# Views outputs multiple display types:
# - Page: renders at a URL like /projects
# - Block: embeds in regions via the Block Layout UI
# - REST export: outputs JSON for decoupled frontends
# - Attachment: attaches data to another display

# Typical Views configuration:
Display: Page
Path: /projects/active
Filter: Content Type = Project Report
Filter: Status = Active (exposed to user)
Sort: Post Date (descending)
Pager: Full pager, 10 per page
Format: Unformatted list of Project Card view modes
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use Views contextual filters (Arguments) to create dynamic views that filter by URL parameters — e.g., /user/[uid]/projects automatically shows only that user's projects!

syllabus.title: Module 4: Custom Module Development
syllabus.desc: Extending Drupal with custom PHP modules using the Hook and Plugin API.
syllabus.content: Custom modules are PHP packages placed in /modules/custom/. Each module requires a .info.yml file (declaring module metadata) and one or more PHP files. Drupal's Hook system lets modules react to core events: hook_node_presave() fires before a node saves, hook_menu_links_discovered_alter() modifies navigation. Plugins extend Drupal's type system with new block types, field formatters, and more.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use drush generate module to scaffold a new custom module with all required files pre-created. It generates the info.yml, module file, routing.yml, and services.yml in seconds!

syllabus.title: Module 5: Theming with Twig Templates
syllabus.desc: Building custom Drupal themes using the Twig templating engine.
syllabus.content: Drupal uses Twig as its templating language — a PHP-based engine with clean {{ variable }}, {% block %}, and {% include %} syntax. Custom themes override core templates by placing identically named .html.twig files in the theme's /templates directory. Theme hook suggestions allow overriding templates for specific content types, view modes, or individual nodes.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Enable Twig debugging in development: set twig_config.debug: true in services.yml. This adds HTML comments showing exact template file names — massively speeding up theme development!

syllabus.title: Module 6: Drupal Security & Access Control
syllabus.desc: Implementing Drupal's role-based permissions and security hardening.
syllabus.content: Drupal's permission system is highly granular. Roles (anonymous, authenticated, editor, administrator) are assigned granular permissions from a matrix of hundreds of options. Access control can be extended programmatically via hook_node_access() and custom access callbacks on routes. Drupal's Security Team actively maintains a security advisory program for all contrib modules.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Never grant the 'administer permissions' permission to non-admin roles — it allows that role to grant itself any other permission, effectively creating a privilege escalation vulnerability!

syllabus.title: Module 7: Drush CLI & Deployment Workflow
syllabus.desc: Managing Drupal from the command line for development efficiency and deployments.
syllabus.content: Drush (Drupal Shell) is the command-line toolkit for managing Drupal. It handles cache clearing, database updates, configuration import/export, module installation, and SQL operations. A deployment workflow typically runs: composer install → drush updatedb → drush config-import → drush cache-rebuild in sequence to safely upgrade a production Drupal site.
syllabus.codeExample:
# Essential Drush commands
drush cr                    # Rebuild all caches
drush cim                   # Import config from YAML files
drush cex                   # Export current config to YAML
drush updatedb              # Run pending database updates
drush en module_name        # Enable a module
drush pmu module_name       # Disable (uninstall) a module
drush sql-dump > backup.sql # Backup database
drush uli                   # Generate one-time admin login link
drush generate block        # Scaffold a custom Block plugin
syllabus.interactiveTip: Run drush deploy as a single deployment command — it runs updatedb, config-import, and cache-rebuild in the correct order. Add it to your CI/CD pipeline to ensure safe automated deployments!

quiz.question: What is the role of a 'View' in Drupal?
options: A PHP class that renders a single node template
A visual query builder that displays lists, tables, or JSON feeds of content
A CSS framework for theming content layouts
A Twig template for the site's homepage
quiz.explanation: Views is Drupal's visual query builder — it fetches content based on configured filters, sorts, and relationships, then displays it as pages, blocks, tables, grids, or REST API endpoints without writing SQL.

quiz.question: Which command rebuilds all Drupal caches via Drush?
quiz.explanation: 'drush cr' (cache:rebuild) is the Drupal 8/9/10 command that rebuilds the service container, routing system, and all cache bins. It is the modern replacement for 'drush cc all' from Drupal 7.

quiz.question: Where should all Drupal customizations (modules and themes) be placed?
quiz.explanation: Custom code always goes in /modules/custom/ and /themes/custom/. The /core directory is managed by Composer and overwritten on updates. /contrib directories are for downloaded community packages.

quest.title: Project: Build a Report Content Type
quest.challenge: Design and configure a complete Drupal content model for project reports.
instructions: 1. Create a 'Report' content type with fields: Title, Body, Priority (select list), Category (term reference), and Report Date.
2. Export the configuration to YAML using drush cex.
3. Create a View that displays all Reports filtered by Priority (exposed filter).
4. Create an 'Editor' role with permission to create and edit only Report content.
5. Override the node--report.html.twig template to add a status badge to the header.
